title: On-Time Shipping Guarantee Terms and Delay Notices — Factory Production Orders
content:
**Terms.** Every change to the projected ship date is recorded as a delay notice with one cause, and the customer is told of it before the ship-notification lead time. When an order already carries the escalation number of delay notices, a further delay is escalated to the production manager and no credit or date promise beyond the recorded notices is made by support. The on-time guarantee applies only to classes that carry it. An on-time guarantee credit is earned only by an order whose build class carries the guarantee. Lateness is measured from the guarantee benchmark date, which is the committed ship date moved later only by delays with an excluded cause; delays from glass supply or factory capacity never move it. The order ships when its last unit ships. Shipping on or before the end of the grace period earns nothing.

These terms cover all Factory Production Orders; the escalation count, the ship-notification lead time, whether a class carries the guarantee, its grace period, credit rate and cap, and the excluded causes are figures of the order's build class.

## Retired clauses

The following two sentences are **no longer in force** and are superseded by the current basis for on-time guarantee credits:

1. "The full calendar weeks late are the calendar days from the benchmark date plus the class grace period (in business days) to the ship date, divided by seven and rounded down."
2. "When at least one full week late results, the order earns, on its ship date, the class credit per unit per week times the units on the order (units remade are counted once and earn nothing for their own remake time), never more than the class cap per order."

## Delay causes

A delay notice carries exactly one cause: glass supplier, factory capacity, weather and freight, customer hold, late acknowledgment, or customer specification remake.

| Cause | Moves the guarantee benchmark |
|---|---|
| customer hold, late acknowledgment, customer specification remake, weather and freight (the excluded causes) | yes — the benchmark is the later of the committed ship date and the latest revised ship date among these notices |
| glass supplier, factory capacity | never |

## Escalation

The delay notices counted for escalation are all of the order's delay notices, of every cause. When the order already carries the class escalation number of delay notices, the next delay goes to the production manager, and support makes no credit or date promise beyond the notices on record.

## Guarantee eligibility

The guarantee is decided by the build class shown on the factory order record. An order in a class that does not carry the guarantee earns no on-time guarantee credit, however late it ships.

## Hypothetical illustration of the benchmark

An order's committed ship date is a Friday. A factory capacity notice later moves its current ship date two weeks later, and a customer hold notice records a revised ship date one week after the committed date. The benchmark is the customer hold notice's revised date, one week after the committed date; the factory capacity notice does not move it.

When at least one full week late results, the order earns, on its ship date, the class credit per unit per week times the units on the order (units remade are counted once and earn nothing for their own remake time), never more than the class cap per order.
